title: ViewModel, UI state, and one-way data flow

videos.script: Until now the planner's screen kept its own state, and the phone could take it away. This lesson gives the state an owner. {{state}} First, one value for one screen. A list of sessions, a total, a count, and what the student is typing. One class describes all of it, and only the ViewModel makes new ones. {{flow}} Then the direction. State goes down to the screen. Events come up from it. The screen draws and never edits. {{rotate}} Then the rotation. A test turns the phone, in effect, and prints who survived. A new activity, and the same ViewModel. {{process}} Then the harder case. The system kills the process in the background. The ViewModel goes with it, and only a small saved bundle comes back. {{leak}} Then what a ViewModel must never hold, and the linter that catches it. {{test}} And last, tests that run in milliseconds, because the ViewModel holds nothing from Android.
